title: Notitia is prerequisite, not a constitutive part of faith — against Bucanus, with Ames and Wittich
source_text: XCIII. Quod attinet ad partes, sive actus fidei, vidimus quoque Scholae Reformatae Doctores inter se non consentire, qui & quales illi sint, eosque pluribus modis enumerare. Et primo quidem quaeritur de notitia, prout ab assensu distinguitur, & significat quandam rei, quae ad credendum proponitur, apprehensionem & praeconceptionem, an sit pars fidem constituens, ut Bucanus & alii censent; an vero solum actus ad fidem praerequisitus & antecedaneus, quae est sententia Guilielmi Amesii, & Christophori Wittichii. Ad quam posteriorem sententiam accedimus. Quamvis enim nemo rite credere possit, qui non habeat aliquam notitiam & conceptionem rei quae credenda est, fides tamen non consistit in illa notitia, quae sine ulla fide in aliquo consistere potest, & inest etiam mentibus prorsus profanis, & in qua nemo possit vere dicere, vel minimum esse fidei initium. Siquidem multi Athei non ignorant quae sint illa quorum fides a Christianis exigitur.
pass_a_gloss: As to the parts, or acts, of faith, we have also seen that the Doctors of the Reformed School do not agree among themselves who and of what sort they are, and enumerate them in many ways. And first indeed it is asked concerning knowledge, as distinguished from assent, and signifying a certain apprehension and preconception of the thing which is proposed to be believed, whether it is a constitutive part of faith, as Bucanus and others judge; or whether only an act prerequisite and antecedent to faith, which is the opinion of William Ames and Christopher Wittich. To which latter opinion we accede. For although no one can rightly believe who does not have some knowledge and conception of the thing which is to be believed, yet faith does not consist in that knowledge, which can exist in someone without any faith, and is present even in wholly profane minds, and in which no one can truly say there is even the least beginning of faith. Inasmuch as many Atheists are not ignorant of those things of which faith is required from Christians.
pass_b_english: Notitia (apprehension of what is to be believed), apart from assent: constitutive part (Bucanus) or only prerequisite (Ames, Wittich)?
Le Blanc sides with Ames/Wittich: you cannot rightly believe without some notion, but faith does not consist in that notion.
Bare notitia can sit in profane minds — even atheists know what Christians are told to believe — without a spark of faith.

lemmas.gloss: knowledge … a constitutive part of faith
an act prerequisite and antecedent to faith

choices.english: To which latter opinion we accede
choices.why: Le Blanc with Ames/Wittich against constitutive notitia.
rejected: Notitia is itself the essence of faith
